## Issue

# Validate tool input against the registered inputSchema

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#37
Labels: priority:medium, type:feature, size:M, area:tools, epic:extension-points

Part of #35

## Why

`ToolRegistry.execute` looks a tool up, logs the input's key names, and calls the executor
without ever checking the declared `inputSchema` (`src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`).
Every tool declares a JSON Schema (`src/types/ai.ts`) that is handed verbatim to both
providers, but nothing validates what comes back from the model. The shipped example shows the
shape of the problem: `example/weather-tool.ts` declares `location` as a required string, then
casts and defaults it (`(input.location as string) || 'Unknown'`) with a comment warning the reader
that `inputSchema` shapes what the model sends but does not enforce it. That is the careful version,
written by the people who wrote the engine — and it still answers a malformed call with a
confidently formatted forecast for `'Unknown'` rather than telling the model it got the call wrong.

The registry currently pushes this check onto each tool's own executor, leaving every consumer
to implement it itself — differently each time, or not at all. A tool that receives unexpected input must fail
in one predictable, known way before the rest of this epic's tool work can be built on top
of it.

## What to do

Validate `input` against the resolved tool definition's `inputSchema` inside
`ToolRegistry.execute`, before the executor runs, using a JSON Schema validator (`ajv`
unless the build proves otherwise) added to `dependencies` — not a second, hand-written
schema in a different format, since the schema already has to match what is handed to the
providers.

Compile a static tool's schema once at `register` time so a broken schema fails at startup,
not mid-conversation; a schema produced by a function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource`
resolves and compiles per call, cached by the resolved schema object.

A rejection returns a `ToolResponse` (`{result: '<what was wrong>'}`) rather than throwing,
so a malformed call becomes something the model can read and correct within the existing
`DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 5` budget, instead of ending the whole conversation with a
generic transport error. Validation enforces `required`, declared types and `enum` only —
it does not inject `additionalProperties: false`, coerce types, or apply defaults, and
there is no opt-out flag.

Update `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `README.md` and `.specify/spec.md` to match.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against the resolved definition's
      `inputSchema` before calling the executor; on failure it returns a `ToolResponse`
      whose `result` describes the failure, and the executor is never invoked
- [ ] A new `src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts` (the registry has no test file today)
      registers a tool requiring a `location` string, calls `execute` with `{}`, and
      asserts the returned result names `location` as required and the executor's call
      count is `0`
- [ ] A test asserts valid input with an unlisted extra property is passed through to the
      executor unchanged (`toEqual`, so an added default or coerced value fails the test) —
      exactly once
- [ ] A test asserts a wrong-typed field (a number where a string is required) is rejected
      with a message naming the field path and the expected type, and that the message does
      **not** contain the offending value
- [ ] A test asserts `register` throws at registration time for an uncompilable schema, and
      that the thrown message names the tool
- [ ] A test asserts a function-valued tool definition whose returned schema differs between
      calls is validated against the schema current at that call, not a stale cached one
- [ ] A test asserts a static tool's schema is compiled once across ten `execute` calls
- [ ] A tool-loop test in `chatOrchestrator.test.ts` drives a stub provider through a
      rejected tool call followed by a corrected retry, and asserts `processMessage`
      resolves — not rejects — with the rejection text visible to the provider on the next
      round
- [ ] `execute` still throws `Unknown tool: <name>` for an unregistered name, unchanged,
      pinned by a test

      that failed, and never a property **value**. Tool input is where identifying data
      enters the engine and the engine redacts nothing today. A test asserts a rejected
      payload containing an identifying field produces no log line and no returned text
      containing that field's value

      `(at)param`/`(at)returns`/`(at)throws` block — and the full contract (rejection `ToolResponse` for input
      the schema rejects, throw only for an unknown tool name) is stated in
      `specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md`, which the comment points at

      spec edits are part of this issue rather than a follow-up

- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`)

## Tech notes

Today's `throw` in `registry.ts` propagates through the orchestrator's tool-call
`Promise.all`, out of the processing loop's `try`, fires `onError`, and reaches the
WebSocket error handler, which sends a generic "Failed to process message" and never sends
the stream-end frame. That end-to-end path is why a rejection has to be a returned
`ToolResponse` instead of a throw.

Deliberately out of scope: the `Unknown tool: <name>` throw stays as-is — the same failure
class handled the opposite way, which is an intentional split, but changing it affects
direct callers and is tracked as *Return an unknown tool name to the model instead of
throwing*. Also out of scope: validating tool *output*; hallucination detection and an
evaluation harness; per-tool authorization — a schema-valid call for someone else's data is still
valid, and authorization is a separate `ToolContext` boundary concern that no issue in this epic
owns (*Let a consumer decline a tool call through a `beforeToolCall` hook* is a veto seam, not an
authorization model); retry, timeout
and rate limiting around tool execution; and any actual tool implementation, which is
written against this contract later.

## -0,0 +1,29 ##
+# Tool Input Validation
+
+| Field  | Value                |
+| ------ | -------------------- |
+| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |
+| Status | Implemented          |
+
+`ToolRegistry.execute` validates the caller-supplied `input` against the tool's declared `inputSchema` before invoking the executor. A failure returns a `ToolResponse` describing the constraint violation so the model can read it and attempt a corrected call within the existing tool-round budget; it never throws, because a throw propagates out of the orchestrator's `Promise.all` and ends the whole conversation with a transport error rather than giving the model a chance to recover.
+
+## Validation contract
+
+- `execute` validates `input` against the resolved tool definition's `inputSchema` before calling the executor; on failure it returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` describes the failure, and the executor is never invoked ([validated by: returns a ToolResponse naming the missing required field and does not invoke the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L7)).
+- Valid input passes through to the executor unchanged; extra properties that are present in `input` but absent from the schema are forwarded without modification ([validated by: passes valid input with an extra property through to the executor unchanged](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L30)).
+- Validation enforces `required`, declared types, and `enum` constraints only — it does not inject `additionalProperties: false`, coerce types, or apply defaults ([validated by: passes valid input with an extra property through to the executor unchanged](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L30)).
+- A wrong-typed field is rejected with a message naming the field path and the expected type; the offending value does not appear in the rejection text or in any log line produced during the call ([validated by: rejects a call whose field type is wrong, naming the field path and expected type but not the value](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L50), [validated by: does not include the rejected field value in the returned text or any log line](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L112)).
+- `execute` still throws `Error('Unknown tool: <name>')` for an unregistered name, unchanged — a missing tool name is a programming error in the caller, not a model input to be corrected ([validated by: throws for an unregistered tool name](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L106)).
+
+## Schema compilation
+
+- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time; an uncompilable schema causes `register` to throw synchronously with a message that names the tool, so a broken schema fails at startup rather than mid-conversation ([validated by: throws at register time when the inputSchema is uncompilable and the message names the tool](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L70)).
+- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` is resolved on each `execute` call; the schema validated against is the schema returned by that call, not the one resolved at `register` time ([validated by: validates each call against the schema the definition function returns at that call](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L81)).
+
+## Orchestrator integration
+
+- A validation failure becomes a tool result (not a thrown error), so the orchestrator delivers the rejection text to the model and the model can attempt a corrected call; `DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 5` is the bound that stops a retry cycle from spinning ([validated by: resolves processMessage and makes the validation-rejection text visible to the provider on the next round](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L523)).
+
+## Out of scope
+
+Validating tool output, hallucination detection, per-tool authorisation, retry and rate limiting around tool execution, and the `Unknown tool: <name>` throw becoming a tool result (tracked separately).

+# Tool Input Validation
+
+| Field  | Value                |
+| ------ | -------------------- |
+| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |
+| Status | Shipped              |
+
+Every tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.
+
+## Validation at execute time
+
+- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L14), [acceptance](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16)).
+- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L44), [acceptance](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46)).
+- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults ([validated by: passes through valid input with extra properties unchanged](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L94)).
+- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake ([validated by: still throws Unknown tool for unregistered name](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L236)).
+- When a dynamic tool's `inputSchema` fails to compile at execution time, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` indicating the compilation failure without invoking the executor ([validated by: rejects execution when dynamic schema fails to compile](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L273)).
+- `ToolRegistry.execute` normalizes any response from a tool executor into a `ToolResponse` object, ensuring consistent handling of simple string results and complex responses with client messages ([validated by: normalizes complex tool responses including client messages](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L288)).
+
+## Registry management and introspection
+
+- `ToolRegistry` provides methods to check for tool presence, retrieve tool definitions, and collect prompt instructions or example prompts across all registered tools ([validated by: provides access to registered tools and definitions](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L242)).
+
+## Schema compilation and caching
+
+- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L118), [acceptance](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94)).
+- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema` ([validated by: reuses static validator even if definition schema is mutated](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L136), [validated by: compiles static tool schema exactly once during registration and reuses it](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L206)).
+- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules ([validated by: caches compiled validators for dynamic tools](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L157), [validated by: validates against the current schema for dynamic tools when it changes](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L180)).
+
+## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery
+
+- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112), [validated by: feeds a validation rejection back to the provider in the next round](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L523)).

# Definition of Done

> `ToolRegistry.execute` looks a tool up, logs the input's key names, and calls the executor
> without ever checking the declared `inputSchema` (`src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts`).
> Every tool declares a JSON Schema (`src/types/ai.ts`) that is handed verbatim to both
> providers, but nothing validates what comes back from the model.

**Strategy: `direct`** — `ToolRegistry.register`, `ToolRegistry.execute` and `createChatOrchestrator` already expose the exact entry points this ticket changes, so the acceptance tests call them directly today and fail because schema compilation and input validation are absent.

## Done when these pass

- [x] **rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor** — `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against `inputSchema`, returns a `ToolResponse` naming the missing required property, and does not invoke the executor.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs** — `ToolRegistry.execute` rejects a property with the wrong JSON Schema type without calling the executor, names the failing field path and expected type in `result`, and omits the offending property value from both `result` and emitted log lines.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled** — `ToolRegistry.register` compiles a static `ToolDefinition`'s `inputSchema` once at registration time and throws synchronously naming the tool when the schema is invalid.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`

- [x] **returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round** — `createChatOrchestrator` feeds a schema-rejected tool call's `ToolResponse.result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` without invoking the executor on the invalid call, allowing the model to retry with valid arguments and complete the turn.
  `src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts`
